title: Mobile data price per GB
definition: Average retail price of one gigabyte of mobile data.
notes: Nominal rupees, so part of the fall since 2016 is inflation rather than price competition. TRAI's figure is an average realised rate across bundles rather than a tariff, and headline comparisons of India as 'cheapest in the world' usually cite a different basket.

The Survey's table carries 2014 and 2025 only, so this is a two-point comparison rather than a path — the years in between are not published here and are not guessed at. The 2025 figure is as of September 2025.
Read from the Economic Survey workbook tabchart9, sheet "Chart IX.21". These are the tables behind the Survey's charts, so the series is only as long as the chart needed.

title: Mobile data used per subscriber
definition: Average wireless data consumption per data user per month.
notes: Per data *user*, not per subscriber: people who own a phone but buy no data are outside the denominator, which lifts the average above what an ordinary reading of ‘per subscriber’ would give. The Survey publishes a much longer comparison elsewhere — 0.06 GB a month in 2014 against 25 GB in 2025 — but only as those two endpoints, so it is not spliced onto this series.

The total column, across all network generations. FY25 is published only as an April-to-September part-year and is left out: a seven-month figure on an annual axis reads as a collapse that did not happen.
Read from the Economic Survey workbook tabchart10, sheet "Chart VIII.20", units as printed: (GB). These are the tables behind the Survey's charts, so the series is only as long as the chart needed.

title: Electric vehicles registered
definition: Electric vehicles registered on the VAHAN national register in a financial year.
notes: VAHAN excludes Telangana and Lakshadweep, which do not report to it, so the national figure is a slight undercount. Two- and three-wheelers dominate the count; reading it as a car number overstates the passenger-vehicle transition by an order of magnitude.

The workbook labels this column with no unit. The figures are read as thousands of vehicles, the only reading consistent with their magnitude — a hundred and seventy-four vehicles nationally in FY20 is not a number, and a hundred and seventy-four million is more than the whole vehicle fleet. Treat the level as the Survey's chart value rather than as a VAHAN extract.
Read from the Economic Survey workbook tabchart8, sheet "Chart VIII.15". These are the tables behind the Survey's charts, so the series is only as long as the chart needed.

title: Domestic air passengers
definition: Passengers carried on domestic scheduled flights in a financial year.
notes: Passengers handled at domestic terminals. The sheet also lists April-to-October part-years for FY24 and FY25; both are excluded, and the FY24 part-year in particular would otherwise contradict the full FY24 row directly above it.

title: Recognised startups
definition: Startups recognised by DPIIT, cumulative to the end of the year.
notes: A recognition count, not a count of companies trading. Recognition is an application a founder makes for tax and procurement benefits, so the series measures uptake of a scheme as much as formation of firms, and it never falls because recognitions are not withdrawn when a startup closes.
Read from the Economic Survey workbook tabchart8, sheet "Chart VIII.23". These are the tables behind the Survey's charts, so the series is only as long as the chart needed.

title: Domestic tourist visits
definition: Visits by domestic tourists to states and union territories in a year.
notes: Visits, not visitors: one person touring four states counts four times, and the total exceeds India's population in most years for that reason.

title: Foodgrains production
definition: Total foodgrain output in a crop year.
notes: Read from the Economic Survey workbook tabchart6, sheet "Chart VI.4". These are the tables behind the Survey's charts, so the series is only as long as the chart needed.

title: Horticulture production
definition: Total horticultural output — fruit, vegetables, spices and plantation crops — in a crop year.
notes: Overtook foodgrains by volume in the mid-2010s, which is the single clearest sign of the shift out of cereal monoculture and is rarely the number quoted.
